questions.scenario: Your relatives just landed from Dubai or the USA and brought massive bags full of imported chocolates. What's your first instinct?

options.text: Unpacking the heavy suitcases and organizing exactly where the big boxes will be stored in the house.
Looking at the airport duty-free tags and wondering how much customs duty they avoided paying.
Checking the exotic packaging and thinking about how these foreign flavors would perform if sold in Indian stores.
Calculating how much profit you could make if you sold these imported chocolates to your friends at school.

questions.scenario: Mummy is packing homemade Diwali sweets (Mithai) to send to your cousin studying abroad. How do you help?

options.text: Packing the sweets tightly in plastic boxes and sealing them with layers of brown tape so they don't leak in transit.
Checking the exact weight and looking up international courier rules to ensure the food items don't get seized at the border.
Wondering how many foreign friends your cousin will share it with and if they'll actually love the taste of Indian sweets.
Bargaining with the local DHL/FedEx courier bhaiya to give you the cheapest shipping rate per kg.

questions.scenario: You are looking at a 'Made in China' or 'Made in Vietnam' label on your new jacket or toy. What crosses your mind?

options.text: Thinking about the massive container ships and dock cranes that physically transported this from there to here.
Wondering what the import tax percentage was that the Indian government charged the company for this item.
Comparing the design and quality with local Indian products to figure out why people prefer the imported ones.
Thinking about how you could bulk-buy these directly from the factory at wholesale prices and sell them online in India.

questions.scenario: You go to a beach like Marine Drive, Juhu, or Chennai port and see a massive cargo ship far out in the ocean.

options.text: Getting fascinated by the sheer size of the ship and trying to count how many thousands of heavy containers it can hold.
Wondering which country's flag the ship is flying and which international maritime laws apply while it is in Indian waters.
Imagining what exotic items, gadgets, or clothes the ship is bringing from completely different cultures around the globe.
Wondering who chartered the ship and mentally calculating the millions of rupees worth of cargo inside.

questions.scenario: You want to buy the latest imported iPhone or gaming console. What is your strategy?

options.text: Being fascinated by the logistics of how millions of fragile phones are shipped in secure boxes globally without a single scratch.
Reading articles about why iPhones are cheaper in Dubai than India due to heavy government import duties and GST.
Watching review videos of how teenagers in different countries are reacting to the new features and colors.
Finding out if a relative coming from abroad can bring it for you to save money on the massive price difference.

questions.scenario: You are watching a news segment about the 'Make in India' campaign. What excites you the most?

options.text: Seeing the massive new factories and shipping ports being built in your state to handle heavy cargo.
Analyzing how the new tax rebates and simplified document clearing will legally help Indian businesses export more easily.
Exploring which Indian handicrafts, spices, or clothes have the highest demand in markets like Europe or America.
Planning to start your own agency one day to help local artisans export their goods and earn massive profits in Dollars.

questions.scenario: You are playing a tycoon or city-building game on your phone. What is your ultimate strategy?

options.text: Focusing on building the biggest harbors, warehouses, and transport roads to physically move materials faster.
Ensuring all the city's trade policies and checkpoint rules are set perfectly to maximize your tax collection.
Seeing which goods your virtual citizens want the most and exploring the world map to import those specific items.
Setting up trade routes with other virtual cities to constantly buy cheap and sell high for maximum profit.

questions.scenario: Your family visits a crowded wholesale market like Sadar Bazaar, Crawford Market, or Chickpet. What catches your eye?

options.text: Watching the laborers perfectly load and unload incredibly heavy gunny bags and boxes onto trucks in the narrow lanes.
Noticing if the shopkeepers are actually generating GST bills and wondering about the import documentation for their goods.
Roaming the tiny lanes to spot the latest trending Korean accessories or Chinese gadgets that everyone is buying right now.
Negotiating hard with the wholesaler to give you a massive discount if you promise to buy 50 pieces of an item in bulk.

questions.scenario: You are at a bank or Forex counter with your parents to exchange Indian Rupees for Foreign currency. What do you do?

options.text: Wondering how physical cash and gold reserves are securely transported in armored trucks across international borders.
Looking at the exchange rate display board and trying to understand why the Dollar fluctuates against the Rupee every single day.
Thinking about how much a local coffee or burger would cost in this new currency compared to your favorite local cafe back home.
Figuring out the exact commission the forex dealer is keeping and asking them if they can offer a better exchange rate.

questions.scenario: Papa ordered an international courier but it got stuck at the customs clearance office. How do you react?

options.text: Imagining the massive airport warehouse where thousands of such packages are piled up waiting to be physically sorted.
Carefully reading the KYC email from the courier company to provide the exact Aadhaar and invoice details needed to release it legally.
Getting super curious about what rare or unique international item Papa ordered that isn't easily available in India.
Calling the shipping company's customer care to angrily demand a timeline and threatening to ask for a refund for the delay.

Port_Supervisor.title: The Dock Commander (Port Operations Supervisor)
Port_Supervisor.primary_match_text: You are an action-oriented organizer! You love physical scale, logistics, and watching massive operations run smoothly like clockwork.
Port_Supervisor.day_in_the_life: Standing at massive shipping ports, directing giant cranes, managing hundreds of containers, and making sure cargo ships leave on time safely.
Port_Supervisor.alternative_match_text: Your love for massive operations and coordination would also make you a great Supply Chain Manager, Warehouse Operations Head, or Navy Officer.
Port_Supervisor.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th Any Stream -> BBA in Logistics/Supply Chain Management or B.Sc in Maritime Studies -> Internships at major ports or shipping lines.

Customs_Analyst.title: The Rule Master (Customs & Compliance Analyst)
Customs_Analyst.primary_match_text: You have a sharp, analytical mind! You love details, finding loopholes, and understanding the complex laws and taxes that govern the world.
Customs_Analyst.day_in_the_life: Checking international cargo documents, calculating heavy import taxes, and ensuring no illegal or restricted items cross the Indian border.
Customs_Analyst.alternative_match_text: Your eye for detail and love for rules would also make you an excellent Tax Consultant, Corporate Lawyer, or Financial Auditor.
Customs_Analyst.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th Commerce -> B.Com or BBA -> Clear the Customs Broker examination (CBLR) by the Government of India or pursue CA/CS.

Market_Researcher.title: The Trend Explorer (Global Market Researcher)
Market_Researcher.primary_match_text: You are a creative explorer! You are deeply curious about different cultures, and what people in other countries like, eat, and buy.
Market_Researcher.day_in_the_life: Traveling virtually (or literally) across the globe, researching if Indian spices will sell well in Japan, or if Korean skincare will work in India.
Market_Researcher.alternative_match_text: Your curiosity about people and trends would also make you a fantastic Marketing Strategist, Consumer Psychologist, or Cultural Anthropologist.
Market_Researcher.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th Humanities/Commerce -> BBA or BA in Economics/Psychology -> MBA in International Marketing or International Business.

Export_Business_Owner.title: The Global Hustler (Freight Forwarder / Export Business Owner)
Export_Business_Owner.primary_match_text: You are a born negotiator and business leader! You love making deals, calculating profits, and trading on a massive global scale.
Export_Business_Owner.day_in_the_life: Calling clients in Dubai, negotiating shipping rates with airlines, and exporting tons of Indian garments or handicrafts for a massive profit.
Export_Business_Owner.alternative_match_text: Your leadership and negotiation skills make you perfect for roles like Entrepreneur, Investment Banker, or Sales Director.
Export_Business_Owner.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th Commerce -> BBA in International Business or B.Com -> Diploma in Export-Import Management from IIFT (Indian Institute of Foreign Trade).
